match.reason: The bank point 'Simple machines' only briefly covers a single fixed pulley changing direction and is a broad overview across levers and inclined planes, so it lacks the multiple-pulley force reduction and the wheel and axle that this point teaches.

draft.title: Pulleys and the wheel and axle
card: Fixed pulley
A single fixed pulley is a wheel with a rope over it, held in one place. It changes the direction of the force, so you pull down to lift a load up. It does not make the force smaller.
More pulleys
Using more pulleys, with some moving with the load, shares the load between more rope sections. This reduces the effort needed. You must pull more rope to lift the load the same height.
Wheel and axle
A wheel and axle is a large wheel fixed to a small rod, the axle, so they turn together. A small force on the rim of the wheel turns the axle with a larger force.

A doorknob is a wheel and axle. You turn the wide knob with a small force, and the thin axle turns the latch with a bigger force. Turning the wheel moves its rim through a longer distance than the axle moves.
draft.remember: A fixed pulley changes direction. More pulleys cut the effort. A wheel and axle makes a small force larger.

a.q: Kai hoists a flag up a pole by pulling down on a rope that runs over a single fixed pulley at the top. What does the pulley do?
opts: Changes the direction of his pulling force
Makes the force needed much smaller
Turns a small force into a larger one
Shares the flag's weight between more ropes
a.why: A single fixed pulley lets Kai pull down to lift the flag up, so it changes the direction of the force. It does not reduce the effort, because only one rope section holds the load. Using less force needs more pulleys.
a.clue: Which way does Kai pull, and which way does the flag move?

b.q: Priya turns the large steering wheel on a boat. Why does a wheel and axle make turning the thin shaft easier?
opts: A small force on the rim becomes a larger force at the axle
A large force on the axle becomes a smaller force at the rim
The wheel changes the direction of the force only
The wheel and axle share the load across more rope
b.why: The wheel is larger than the axle, so a small force on its rim turns the axle with a larger force. The second option reverses cause and effect. Sharing a load over more rope belongs to a system of pulleys, not a wheel and axle.
b.clue: Think about the doorknob: which part do your fingers turn?

wants.brief: Two diagrams side by side. Left: a single fixed pulley fixed to a beam, with a rope over it, a load hanging on one side and an arrow labelled effort pulling down on the other. Right: a pulley system with two pulleys, one fixed to the beam and one moving with the load, with the rope sections holding the load marked and an arrow labelled effort. Label: fixed pulley, moving pulley, rope, load, effort.
wants.why: Seeing the rope sections helps students understand how more pulleys share the load.

a.best: Changes the direction of his pulling force

b.best: A small force on the rim becomes a larger force at the axle

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'The second option reverses cause and effect'. Options are shown in random order, so 'second option' may point to the wrong choice. The reversed option (a large force on the axle becoming a smaller force at the rim) also swaps where the force is applied; it does not reverse cause and effect. Name the option by its content instead.
